=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text names "map|compass|water|sandwich|glucose|tin|banana|apple|cheese|beer|suntan cream|camera|T-shirt|trousers|umbrella|waterproof trousers|waterproof overclothes|note-case|sunglasses|towel|socks|book"
text data "9 150 13 35 153 200 50 160 15 60 68 45 27 60 39 40 23 30 52 10 11 70 32 30 24 15 48 10 73 40 42 70 43 75 22 80 7 20 18 12 4 50 30 10"
text tw "total weight "
text tv "total value "
global vals long 44
global best long 401
global keep uchar 9223
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note parse reads the decimal numbers in s (separated by spaces, an optional - sign) into vals and
note returns how many; one pass over s, so the loop is bounded by len s
fn parse s view uchar * to ulong
n = ulong 0
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
for i ulong len s
c = get s i
if eq c 45
sg = long -1
else
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 long sub c 48
dig = true
else
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
end
end
end
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
ret n
end
note item writes the k-th name of the |-separated names text
fn item k ulong to void
f = ulong 0
st = ulong 0
for i ulong len names
if eq get names i 124
if eq f k
emit part names st sub i st
ret
end
f = add f 1
st = add i 1
end
end
emit part names st sub len names st
end
note pack runs the 0-1 dynamic program over capacities 0..400: best[c] is the best value with weight <= c
note using the items seen so far; keep[i*401+c] records that item i was taken at capacity c
fn pack n ulong to void
for i ulong n
w = ulong get vals mul i 2
v = get vals add mul i 2 1
for x ulong 401
c = sub 400 x
if ge c w
if gt add get best sub c w v get best c
put best c add get best sub c w v
put keep add mul i 401 c 1
end
end
end
end
end
fn main to int
n = div parse data 2
pack n
note walk back from capacity 400 over the items in reverse, taking each recorded item
c = ulong 400
tot = ulong 0
for x ulong n
i = sub sub n x 1
if eq get keep add mul i 401 c 1
put vals add mul i 2 1 -1
w = ulong get vals mul i 2
c = sub c w
tot = add tot w
end
end
for i ulong n
if eq get vals add mul i 2 1 -1
item i
emit nl
end
end
emit tw
emitu tot
emit nl
emit tv
emiti get best 400
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
map
compass
water
sandwich
glucose
banana
suntan cream
waterproof trousers
waterproof overclothes
note-case
sunglasses
socks
total weight 396
total value 1030
</pre>
